newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs mostly steady-up $1-private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs mostly steady-up $1-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold Monday at prices mostly steady to $1.00 per cwt higher compared with Friday's top prices, lifted by light hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Marketings were further reduced by heat and humidity in the western Corn Belt, they said.
"It's not a big factor yet, because you can still get hogs in early enough, but numbers are still a problem, there's just not enough to go around," a central Iowa hog buyer said.
Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $56.50-$57.00 in the country and $57.00-$58.50 at plants, dealers there said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, with gains powered by limited marketings from heat and humidity, sources said.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower early at $57.00 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 at plants, but could turn higher if marketings slow, buyers there said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants.
